## What the chronicles say [Record]

Modern accounts (Wikipedia's civil-war article, citing Ivinskis, Urban, Kiaupa; VLE, Kęstutis and Skirgaila) put it on **3 August 1382**. Trakai had surrendered to Jogaila and the Order on 20 July; the armies of [Kęstutis](../characters/kestutis.qmd) and [Jogaila](../characters/jogaila.qmd) then stood facing each other near [Trakai](../places/trakai.qmd). [Skirgaila](../characters/skirgaila.qmd) persuaded Kęstutis and [Vytautas](../characters/vytautas.qmd) to come to the talks at [Jogaila's camp near Trakai](../places/jogaila_camp_trakai.qmd), where both were treacherously arrested, and taken to [Krėva](../places/kreva.qmd). No battle was fought. Some accounts place the arrest closer to 10 August; the sources count from the arrest to Kęstutis's death on 15 August ("a week later", or two weeks). The tradition that Skirgaila guaranteed a safe-conduct is plausible but not in a named chronicle. Principal sources are the Order's chroniclers (Wigand of Marburg, Johann von Posilge) and the later Lithuanian chronicles.

## What really happened [Saga]

A treachery under sworn safety is the oath-break Perkūnas notes: Skirgaila's oath on Perkūnas, given at Trakai two weeks earlier, is the safe-conduct. Book I stages it where the record puts it. The camp's iron-bound palisade gate, built by the Order's carpenters, shuts behind the ducal retinue; sound dies in the camp (the Shadow-Seller's Breath of the Void); hundreds of archers line the palisade; Skirgaila speaks from the wooden balcony of the negotiating hall (a requisitioned manor), Jogaila watches from the upper gallery, and [Henė](../characters/hanulas.qmd) turns one blackened stone under the gate beams. The same night Skirgaila's men massacre Kęstutis's guard in the tents beyond the manor fence, blocking the tent openings while Jogaila sits alone at a feast; [seven of the hidden nine die and are buried in the bog](../factions/iron_wolves.qmd), while Jonas's men stayed in Kęstutis's own camp.

## Consequences

The arrest follows [Jogaila's retaking of Vilnius](ev_vilnius_retaken.qmd) and leads directly to [Kęstutis's death at Krėva](ev_kestutis_death.qmd). Vytautas, who escapes Krėva in the autumn, carries the story forward.

## Dramatisation

Book I ch. 4 "Kelionė į stovyklą" (the ride to the camp; [the Beggar](ev_beggar_coin.qmd) on the road, 3 August), ch. 5 "Dvigubas Veidas" (Jogaila, same day, the requisitioned Trakai manor), ch. 6 "Geležiniai Vartai" (the "Iron Gates" are the camp palisade gate; late-summer afternoon), ch. 7 "Tylos Puota" (Jogaila and Skirgaila; the same night). Kęstutis's body is still burned in Vilnius (ch. 10).
